⚠ these are the Section A (static GEP) InVEST SDR settings, taken from build_args where they were hardcoded. The DYNAMIC shock path in erosion_sdr uses a different set: threshold_flow_accumulation 1000 rather than 100, sdr_max 0.8 rather than 0.5, ic_0_param 0.5 rather than 0.8. sdr_max and ic_0_param are transposed between the two, which looks like a transcription error rather than a decision. Both are written out here rather than merged, because merging them would change a number; whoever knows which calibration is intended should settle it.

threshold_high 11.0 t/ha/yr is the SES-11 severe-erosion threshold the account is named for, and threshold_low 2.0 the tolerable one. They decide which pixels count as severe, so they are the two rows most worth checking against the methodology before a run.
0.08 is the fallback yield response used when a crop has no row in the elasticity table. 19 of 46 crops take it, and 5 crops have no entry at all, so it is doing more work than a fallback should.

every flood input is a get_path reference under base_data, the same way terrestrial_carbon and the rest resolve theirs. The pipeline used to build all of them by hand from a flood_root_dir, which is not how ProjectFlow finds data. outputs are named by the task that writes them, under its own cur_dir, so nothing here points at a results location.

protection_path and protection_evidence_path are optional companions: blank means the table is not supplied, and the readers branch on None. When an evidence table IS given and has no ISO3 column the run stops, because which countries count as documented decides how much damage is truncated.

⚠ flood_tasks reads this with TWO different defaults -- False at the run_valuation_chain call site and True at the GEP one -- so the behaviour depended on which ran. The damage tables are prebuilt inputs and the inputs directory is not writable, so building them raises PermissionError; the deleted set_flood_paths set True. Setting it here makes both call sites agree

⚠ apply_service_flow and report_protection_split are TRUE here and FALSE as getattr defaults in configure_valuation. The deleted set_flood_paths set both True, so the run behaviour was True while the code default said otherwise. Deleting it without moving these would have silently turned off the ecosystem attribution that produces ead_attributed_to_spa_usd2019

the source author's pipeline. The GEP value raster is his output, not a construction of ours: CropGrids harvested area times a Monfreda within-country yield pattern times FAO calibration. The raster is staged into base_data by hand when a base year he has not published is needed; docs/runbook_pollination_value_raster.md has the six commands. Deliberately not automated: running his pipeline from ours would make this the only task in the library that executes another repository code
